issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אַחְבִּירָה עֲלֵיכֶם בְּמִלִּים' means 'I would join/string together words against you' (i.e., speak forcefully against you), not 'I would make a covenant with you in words' (立約). The verb חָבַר means 'to join/associate', not 'to covenant' (בְּרִית). This changes the meaning from adversarial speech to a covenant-making act.

The Hebrew 'וְאָנִיעָה עֲלֵיכֶם בְּמוֹ רֹאשִׁי' means 'and I would shake my head at you' (a gesture of scorn/mockery), not 'and I swear by my head' (以我的頭起誓). The verb נוּעַ means 'to shake/move to and fro', not 'to swear'. This changes the gesture from derision to an oath.
